thread.title: Netflix earnings send stock surging, suggest huge decline was 'an aberration'

author: morningstar.com
title: Netflix earnings send stock surging, suggest huge decline was 'an aberration'
text:
By Sarah Toy
Netflix subscriber growth far surpasses expectations after big miss last quarter sent stock into nosedive
Investors wasted no time after Netflix Inc. (NFLX) announced it beat third-quarter earnings expectations Tuesday afternoon, sending shares of the streaming giant up 12% in after-hours trading.
Netflix reported adding a net 6.96 million subscribers in the most recent quarter, with 1.09 million coming from the U.S. and 5.87 million coming from overseas, soundly beating the FactSet consensus of 5.32 million and the company's own forecast of 5 million. Netflix missed subscriber growth expectations last quarter, which sent the stock into a nosedive (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-stock-slammed-after-second-quarter-subscriber-numbers-and-revenue-fall-short-2018-07-16).
"One of the big questions after they missed the earnings and membership numbers in Q2 was whether it was just an aberration or a sign of weakening business," Forrester principal analyst Jim Nail said. "These numbers show that it was clearly an aberration."
Net income for the third quarter rose to $403 million, or 89 cents a share, from $129.6 million, or 29 cents a share, in the same quarter a year ago. The FactSet consensus for the third quarter was 68 cents a share. Revenue rose to $4 billion, beating the FactSet consensus of $3.99 billion and up 25% from $2.99 billion a year ago.
Netflix forecast sunny days ahead for the fourth quarter, saying it expects total net additions of 9.4 million and paid net additions of 7.6 million, increases of 13% and 15%, respectively, from the same period last year.
The company's fourth-quarter originals roster includes the final season of "House of Cards" and the debut of "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina," based on the Archie Comics character Sabrina the Teenage Witch. Netflix plans to continue its aggressive spending on original content, estimating that free cash flow will be around negative $3 billion for 2018.
"Our growing mix of self-produced content, which requires us to fund content during the production phase prior to its release on Netflix, is the primary driver of our working capital needs that creates the gap between our positive net income and our free cash flow deficit," company executives wrote in a letter to shareholders.
Some analysts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-earnings-was-the-streaming-giants-second-quarter-miss-really-just-a-blip-2018-10-11) have voiced concern about Netflix's aggressive use of debt to finance its free cash flow deficits, especially in an environment of rising interest rates, though for now it seems most investors won't mind the negative free cash flow as long as subscriber numbers continue to grow.
For concerned investors, the streaming giant also explained why it continues to spend so much on content.
"We want to maximize the size of our membership base and people have very diverse tastes that we seek to satisfy," the letter said. "This also reduces our dependence on any individual title. Even our largest titles, which are viewed by tens of millions of our members, only account for a low single digit percentage of total streaming hours."
Netflix acknowledged the rise of content competitors like AT&T Inc.'s (T) WarnerMedia and The Walt Disney Co. (DIS), as well as tech companies like Apple Inc. (AAPL) and Amazon.com, Inc (AMZN) .
"Amid these massive competitors on both sides, plus traditional media firms, our job is to make Netflix stand out so that when consumers have free time, they choose to spend it with our service," the company wrote.
Netflix stock was still feeling the effects of the post-earnings decline last quarter, having fallen 13.5% in the past three months. The S&P 500 index gained 0.4% in that period.
-Sarah Toy;
